title: Turning a phage anti-defense weapon into an immunity trigger
content:
by Anna B. Adelstein, Naama Aviram

Most bacterial immune systems raise an alarm when they sense a phage. A new study in PLOS Biology shows how type II Panoptes reverses this logic by maintaining a quiet signal and sensing infection through its sudden disappearance.
